solutions.check: 26 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Advance screening of source of Putin's appraisal

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the Russian president's name
an appraisal is an assessment or critique

explanation.surface: A sneak look at what the Russian president thinks of something, before anyone else sees it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay; 'Putin's appraisal' looks like one idea but splits into a single letter and a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or show shown to critics or the public before its official release is called this.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Be prepared to shoot naked members, it's said

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the words are matched by sound

blocks.note: naked means bare and members are limbs

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of someone ready to photograph nudists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' tempts a photography reading, but here it means fire a gun. The answer runs across 2 and 24 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry weapons, the phrase from the US Second Amendment, is to be armed and ready to fire.

clue.text: Wicked hotel pro who explores down below

definitions.note: a clause standing for 'one who explores down below', a noun

indicators.note: something wicked has gone wrong or bad, so the letters are corrupted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters

explanation.surface: A naughty hotel sex worker whose speciality is below the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down below' suggests something rude; the definition is really about going underground into caves.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for a caver, someone who explores underground cave systems and potholes as a sport.

clue.text: Stick tip of todger in Posy – make a meal of it

indicators.note: a tip is an extreme end, here the far end of the word, so its last letter is kept
to stick one thing into another places it inside, which the following 'in' confirms

blocks.note: the final letter of this slang word
a posy is a small bunch of flowers

explanation.surface: Putting the end of a penis in a woman called Posy and making a fuss about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A todger is British slang for a penis. Its tip here is its last letter, not the first, and 'make a meal of it' (overdo it) hides the bare definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-morning combination of breakfast and lunch eaten as a single sitting at the table.

clue.text: Positive aspect associated with bum fluff being inverted?

blocks.note: the good side of a situation
down is soft fine hair, the wispy first beard of a youth

explanation.surface: Looking on the bright side of fuzz on the backside when you are standing on your head.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum fluff is British slang for a teenager's first sparse facial hair; 'bum' makes it sound anatomical, but both parts just mean soft fine hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned over so its top is at the bottom is said to be the wrong way up.

clue.text: Like Brenda, on occasion, boasted about "one's focus"

indicators.note: a focus is a central point, so the middle letter is kept
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to crow is to brag
the central letter of this three-letter word

explanation.surface: The Queen, on certain days, bragged about her personal interests.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II; 'one's' mimics the royal way of speaking but just means the middle of 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch wore the crown on state occasions, so at such times she had a crown on her head.

clue.text: Licence form falsified and filled out by press boss hoarding energy

indicators.note: falsified means tampered with, so the letters are altered in order
something filled out by material has that material placed inside it
to hoard is to keep stored inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the editor runs a newspaper; ED is the standard abbreviation
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A forged licence application completed by a newspaper editor who is stockpiling power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like part of the definition (a licence form) but is the anagram fodder; FROM is split open to take ED, which already holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence in the sense of liberty to act as one pleases, unrestrained, is a synonym of liberty.

clue.text: Coach provides agent with all-over shave

indicators.note: something all over another surrounds it on every side

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
to pare is to trim or shave thinly

explanation.surface: A sports coach arranges a full-body wax for a players' agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-over shave' reads as a body depilation, but 'all-over' tells you to wrap the shave around the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to train them up and get them ready for an exam or event.

clue.text: Academic on 'a loud-mouthed, hollow, ultimately corrupt arse and bad loser'

indicators.note: hollow means emptied out, so only the outside letters remain
ultimately means in the end, so just the final letter is taken

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written
the first and last letters of this compound word
the final letter of this word
rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A professor's withering verdict on a brash, empty, crooked fool who can't accept defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The insults read as pure description, but each one quietly supplies letters; 'on' places the academic above the rest in this down clue, and the final phrase points at the 2020 election refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The US president famously refused to concede his 2020 election defeat, making him the poster figure for sore losing.

clue.text: A load of balls by cast that's utterly defeated

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
cast and thrown are past participles of hurl

explanation.surface: Calling a show's performers rubbish and declaring them thoroughly beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A load of balls' is British slang for nonsense, and 'cast' suggests actors; in cricket, an over is the six balls a bowler delivers in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A government or ruler that has been toppled and removed from power has been completely beaten.

clue.text: State of independence that hurt one

blocks.note: I is a standard abbreviation for independent or independence
the cry of someone in pain
a means one, as in 'a dog'

explanation.surface: A newly independent country feeling the pain of its separation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of independence' sounds like a single political idea; 'that hurt' is an exclamation, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: This Midwestern territory is one of the fifty constituent members of the United States of America.

clue.text: In awe, as elected treacherous type

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters straddles the three words

explanation.surface: Voters gaze in admiration at the person they've chosen, who turns out to be a backstabber.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' looks like part of a phrase 'in awe', but it tells you the answer is inside the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone this small predator figuratively means they are sly, sneaky and not to be trusted.

clue.text: Not getting any dessert that's been mixed with vax

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; vax is slang for vaccine

explanation.surface: Missing out on pudding because it has been laced with vaccine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not getting any' seems to refer to the dessert, but it is the idiom for having no sex.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not getting any' is a slang idiom for going without intercourse, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Who succeeds in crushing her with a vice

definitions.note: a clause standing for 'one who succeeds', a noun

indicators.note: crushing something breaks it up, so the letters are smashed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets ahead by squashing a woman in a workshop clamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a vice' suggests a tool or a bad habit; 'with' joins the two parts of the fodder, and the vice is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accomplishes goals and reaches success is described with this noun for a high performer.

clue.text: Turning over old lover with ceremony

blocks.note: a former partner
a customary ritual or established practice

explanation.surface: Rolling over in bed beside a former partner as a sort of ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning over' suggests rolling or flipping; here it means handing someone over to the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing a suspect to the legal authorities of another country for trial is formally called this.

clue.text: Pussy having been rejected, I become reticent

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a pussy is a cat
taken as written
to turn is to become, as in 'turn sour'

explanation.surface: After being turned down for sex, a man goes quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pussy' carries the rude sense in the surface but just means a cat in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone reserved and uncommunicative, saying little; they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Bill's position: getting end away on a highway

indicators.note: having an end taken away removes the last letter

blocks.note: a place is a position
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill describing his favourite position: having sex on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply drops the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill in the sense of a printed notice or poster stuck up publicly is a sign of this kind.

clue.text: Dullness of love and sex in smart surroundings

indicators.note: in means placed inside, and 'surroundings' confirms the outer piece wraps round

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, which looks like O
smart in the sense of quick, brisk
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: How boring love and sex become in posh surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' suggests elegance; here it means fast, as in 'at a smart pace'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of brilliance or transparency, a murky obscurity of expression or colour, is what this noun names.

clue.text: Veteran told off by Cyclops (twice) is at end of tether

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the setter refers to himself twice, once as subject and once as object
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: An old soldier, scolded repeatedly by the setter, is at the limit of his patience.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is this puzzle's setter, so he is both I and ME. 'Told off' reads as scolded, but 'off' shuffles the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been around a long time and has plenty of experience is a seasoned old hand.

clue.text: Fair to smear alien?

blocks.note: to smear something is to stain or mark it
E.T. is the alien from Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: Is it just to slander a foreigner?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like an adjective meaning just, but it is the noun for a trading event.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is a gathering of stalls for buying and selling goods, like a bazaar or trading venue.

clue.text: Shady thing, sticking one in parrot

indicators.note: sticking something in another pushes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to parrot is to imitate or copy
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: Some dodgy character stuffing something into a parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady' suggests dishonest, but the definition means giving shade. 'Parrot' is a verb here, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhead covering of cloth or foliage casts shade on whatever lies beneath it, like an awning.

clue.text: Mark's second estate?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
an estate is an estate car, the British name for a station wagon

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark owns a second property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' looks like a man's name with a possessive; it is the definition plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting blemish left on the skin after a wound heals, so it is a kind of mark.

clue.text: Casually terminate Conservative leader, as payment

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so the opening letter is kept
doing something casually is careless and haphazard, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Offhandedly sacking the Tory party leader, as a kind of payback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative leader' reads as a party chief, but it only supplies its first letter to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A remittance is a sum of money sent to someone, often abroad, to settle an account.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Brown-noser providing Tarzan's means of transport

blocks.note: first meaning: a sycophant who sucks up to the boss
second meaning: a climbing vine he swings on through the jungle

explanation.surface: A toady who supplies the jungle hero with his ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown-noser is slang for a crawler or toady; the second meaning is the trailing jungle plant Tarzan swings from.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both an obsequious flatterer and a trailing vine plant that climbs trees.

clue.text: Gibraltar resident, stiffly formal, taking tea perhaps?

blocks.note: prim means stiffly proper
having tea is an example of eating; the tense is loose

explanation.surface: A starchy Gibraltarian sitting down to afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar, the British territory at the tip of Spain, is famous for its colony of Barbary macaques; the clue wants an ape, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbary macaques living on the Rock are monkeys, which belong to this order of mammals.
